question.text: A chain of mass $\mathrm{M}$ is placed on a smooth table with $1 / \mathrm{n}$ of its length $\mathrm{L}$ hanging over the edge. The work done in pulling the hanging portion of the chain back to the surface of the table is

solution.text:
$\quad \mathrm{W}=$ change in $\mathrm{PE}$ of $\mathrm{COM}$ of hanging part
$$
=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{g} \frac{\mathrm{L}}{2 \mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrm{MgL}}{2 \mathrm{n}^{2}}
$$
